title: Stochastic pager filter and multi-region load-shed playbook
creator: Anika Rao
description: Reduce noisy pages from transient SLO violations while enabling deterministic multi-region failover and graceful load shedding. Implement a probabilistic (stochastic) alert filter that suppresses low-value duplicates, wire it into region-aware circuit breakers, and codify an automated runbook for safe partial degradation and rollback.
background: Over the past 6 months we've observed a high volume of low-actionable pager alerts during regional load spikes (see dashboards linked). Many alerts stem from transient tail-latency spikes caused by queueing and cold KV-cache misses; these often resolve within seconds but generate repeated pages across multiple teams and regions. Current threshold-based suppression causes either too many pages or long detection latency that delays mitigation. We need a middle ground: shorten time-to-recovery for real incidents while reducing cognitive load for on-call engineers.
proposal:
1) Implement a stochastic pager filter: each alert candidate is assigned a suppression score based on SLO breach severity, recent similar signals, and business-impact weighting. Alerts with low scores are probabilistically suppressed (lower probability -> more likely to page) using an exponential backoff factor for repeated signals.
2) Tie filter outputs to per-region circuit breakers: when a region's error/latency budget consumption crosses a soft threshold, we flip a staged circuit that changes routing and enables automated shedding measures (prefetch/cache-priority, reject-low-priority-requests).
3) Provide an automated runbook that executes verification checks, triggers controlled traffic shift to secondary regions, performs canary rollback policy, and surfaces human escalation with contextual diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: Stochastic filter implemented and toggleable via feature flag
Filter reduces total pages by >=35% for no-impact transients in beta region (ap-southeast-1) over 2 weeks
Per-region circuit breaker state machine implemented and observable in Console with timestamps and metrics
Automated playbook can execute: health-checks -> partial shed (20%) -> traffic shift (up to 50%) -> rollback within < 6 minutes if errors increase
Comprehensive unit and integration tests for filter, circuit state transitions, and runbook actions
Documentation and runbook available in Console and Confluence; on-call team briefed and runbook exercised in two simulated drills
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged launch to staging; run synthetic noise tests (2 days). 2) Canary in ap-southeast-1 for non-production tenants (1 week). 3) Collect metrics and iterate on filter parameters (2 weeks). 4) Gradual enablement in eu-west-1 and us-west-2 with on-call present. 5) Post-mortem after first live activation and three drills; default suppression policy set to conservative until two green drills.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for suppression logic and backoff math.
- Integration tests simulating multi-region failover and verify traffic steering actions.
- Chaos run: inject transient latency/503s and measure pages generated.
- Drill: full runbook exercise with on-call and SRE, record timings and operator feedback.
